1	"""Confirm one ordinary regular file and open exactly that confirmed file.
2	
3	This is the single file-confirmation rule shared by every entry point
4	that turns a path into sample bytes:
5	
6	* single-file import (``DatasetStore.add``),
7	* whole-directory import (``DatasetStore.import_directory``),
8	* recorded-source export (``export`` without ``--source-dir``), and
9	* ``--source-dir`` export, both when the source tree is looked up and
10	  when the selected copy is streamed into the package.
11	
12	The rule:
13	
14	1. The path is inspected *without following a final symlink*
15	   (``lstat`` / ``fstatat``); the object found there must be a regular
16	   file.  Callers that arrive through their own non-symlink walk
17	   (directory import, source-dir export) only ever confirm such paths,
18	   single-file import resolves a symlink given as its argument before
19	   calling in here, and recorded-source export resolves the recorded
20	   path once (following a symlink present at the start) before the same
21	   confirmation, so following links at the start stays an entry-point
22	   decision.
23	2. The path is opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW`` (relative to a pinned
24	   directory descriptor when the caller has one), so a symlink swapped
25	   onto the path after the inspection cannot redirect the open.  The
26	   open also carries ``O_NONBLOCK``: an object swapped in after the
27	   inspection — a named pipe with no writer, in particular — is opened
28	   (or refused) immediately instead of making the caller wait for data,
29	   and the descriptor is proved to be a regular file on the very next
30	   step, before any byte is read.
31	3. The opened descriptor is ``fstat()``ed and proved to be a regular
32	   file carrying the exact ``(device, inode)`` identity that was
33	   confirmed (or, for the export copy, the identity recorded during the
34	   lookup): a different regular file renamed onto the path — even one
35	   with identical content, size and modification time — is rejected
36	   just like a symlink, even one pointing at the original file, and a
37	   named pipe or other non-regular object caught by the non-blocking
38	   open is rejected the same way.  Only then is the descriptor's
39	   blocking mode restored, so the files callers actually stream behave
40	   exactly like an ordinary blocking open.
41	
42	What differs between entry points deliberately stays outside this
43	module:
44	
45	* whether a path occupied by something else *after* a successful open
46	  still matters — import re-inspects the path once the read is done and
47	  requires the same file with the same size and mtime, while export
48	  keeps reading the already pinned descriptor (the path may be
49	  reoccupied without spoiling the confirmed bytes);
50	* the public exception type, wording and identifying information.
51	
52	Failures are therefore reported as structured :class:`ConfirmationError`
53	reasons; each entry point translates them into its existing public
54	errors, preserving the path, digest and reason information callers rely
55	on.
56	"""
57	
58	from __future__ import annotations
59	
60	import errno
61	import fcntl
62	import hashlib
63	import os
64	import stat
65	from dataclasses import dataclass
66	from enum import Enum
67	from typing import NamedTuple
68	
69	# Samples are streamed in fixed chunks, so large files never need memory
70	# for their whole content; every reader below uses the same chunk size.
71	READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 1024 * 1024
72	
73	# Open without following a final symlink; 0 on platforms lacking the flag.
74	_O_NOFOLLOW = getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
75	# Open without waiting for a writer/reader or carrier: the descriptor is
76	# proved to be a regular file before any read, so an object swapped onto
77	# the path after the inspection — a named pipe with no writer in
78	# particular — is opened (and then rejected) immediately instead of
79	# making the confirmation wait for data.  Cleared again once the open is
80	# proved regular, so streaming sees an ordinary blocking descriptor.
81	_O_NONBLOCK = getattr(os, "O_NONBLOCK", 0)
82	
83	
84	class ConfirmStage(str, Enum):
85	    """Where in the confirm-then-open sequence a failure was detected."""
86	
87	    INSPECT = "inspect"  # the no-follow lstat()/fstatat() before opening
88	    OPEN = "open"  # the O_NOFOLLOW open()
89	    PROVE = "prove"  # the fstat() of the freshly opened descriptor
90	
91	
92	class ConfirmReason(str, Enum):
93	    """What went wrong, independent of the caller's public wording."""
94	
95	    ACCESS_ERROR = "access error"  # an underlying syscall failed; .error set
96	    NOT_REGULAR = "not a regular file"  # a non-symlink, non-regular object
97	    NOW_SYMLINK = "is now a symlink"  # the path became a final symlink
98	    WRONG_IDENTITY = "wrong identity"  # another object occupies the path
99	
100	
101	@dataclass
102	class ConfirmationError(Exception):
103	    """A path could not be confirmed as, or opened as, one stable file.
104	
105	    ``status`` carries the inspection result when one was obtained, so a
106	    caller can tell symlinks from other non-regular objects; ``error``
107	    carries the underlying :class:`OSError` for access failures.
108	    """
109	
110	    reason: ConfirmReason
111	    stage: ConfirmStage
112	    status: os.stat_result | None = None
113	    error: OSError | None = None
114	
115	    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging only
116	        return f"{self.reason.value} at {self.stage.value}"
117	
118	
119	def inspect_regular(
120	    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
121	    *,
122	    dir_fd: int | None = None,
123	    expected: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
124	) -> os.stat_result:
125	    """Inspect ``path`` without following a final symlink and confirm it.
126	
127	    Returns the status of the confirmed regular file.  When ``dir_fd``
128	    is given, ``path`` is interpreted relative to that descriptor
129	    (``fstatat``); otherwise it is ``lstat()``ed directly.
130	
131	    ``expected`` optionally carries the ``(device, inode)`` the binding
132	    must still carry — the identity recorded during the source-dir
133	    lookup when the export copy re-confirms a selected path.  A path
134	    that is a symlink, is not a regular file, or no longer carries the
135	    expected identity raises :class:`ConfirmationError` before anything
136	    is opened.
137	    """
138	    try:
139	        if dir_fd is None:
140	            status = os.lstat(path)
141	        else:
142	            status = os.stat(path, dir_fd=dir_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
143	    except OSError as error:
144	        raise ConfirmationError(
145	            ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, error=error
146	        ) from error
147	    if stat.S_ISLNK(status.st_mode):
148	        raise ConfirmationError(
149	            ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
150	        )
151	    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
152	        raise ConfirmationError(
153	            ConfirmReason.NOT_REGULAR, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
154	        )
155	    if expected is not None and (status.st_dev, status.st_ino) != expected:
156	        raise ConfirmationError(
157	            ConfirmReason.WRONG_IDENTITY, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
158	        )
159	    return status
160	
161	
162	def open_without_follow(
163	    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
164	    *,
165	    dir_fd: int | None = None,
166	    nonblocking: bool = True,
167	) -> int:
168	    """Open ``path`` read-only with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, never following a link.
169	
170	    With ``nonblocking`` (the default) the open also carries
171	    ``O_NONBLOCK``: it never waits for another process, so a named pipe
172	    (or other carrier) swapped onto the path in the gap after the
173	    inspection is opened immediately even with no writer present,
174	    rather than blocking before the descriptor can be proved.  Callers
175	    that pair this open with :func:`prove_opened_regular` get an
176	    ordinary blocking descriptor back once the open is proved regular.
177	    A final symlink swapped in after the inspection makes the open fail
178	    with ``ELOOP``, which is reported as
179	    :class:`ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK` rather than a generic access
180	    error; every other open failure carries the original
181	    :class:`OSError`.  The descriptor belongs to the caller on success.
182	
183	    ``nonblocking=False`` restores the plain blocking
184	    ``O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW`` open for callers that deliberately keep the
185	    historical lookup-open semantics (the source-directory scan); such
186	    callers must not rely on the descriptor being proved here.
187	    """
188	    flags = os.O_RDONLY | _O_NOFOLLOW
189	    if nonblocking:
190	        flags |= _O_NONBLOCK
191	    try:
192	        return os.open(path, flags, dir_fd=dir_fd)
193	    except OSError as error:
194	        reason = (
195	            ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK
196	            if error.errno == errno.ELOOP
197	            else ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR
198	        )
199	        raise ConfirmationError(
200	            reason, ConfirmStage.OPEN, error=error
201	        ) from error
202	
203	
204	def _clear_nonblocking(descriptor: int) -> None:
205	    """Restore ordinary blocking semantics on a proved descriptor.
206	
207	    The non-blocking flag only existed to keep the open itself from
208	    waiting on a swapped non-regular carrier; streaming the now-proved
209	    regular file must behave like an ordinary blocking open.  Clearing
210	    access flags on a regular file never blocks.
211	    """
212	    try:
213	        flags = fcntl.fcntl(descriptor, fcntl.F_GETFL)
214	        fcntl.fcntl(descriptor, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags & ~os.O_NONBLOCK)
215	    except OSError as error:
216	        _close_quietly(descriptor)
217	        raise ConfirmationError(
218	            ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR, ConfirmStage.PROVE, error=error
219	        ) from error
220	
221	
222	def prove_opened_regular(
223	    descriptor: int, confirmed: os.stat_result
224	) -> os.stat_result:
225	    """Prove ``descriptor`` is the confirmed regular file itself.
226	
227	    The descriptor is ``fstat()``ed and must be a regular file carrying
228	    ``confirmed``'s ``(device, inode)``; this covers the object that is
229	    actually read, not just one look at the path before it was opened.
230	    A named pipe or other non-regular object that the non-blocking open
231	    let through after a swap — even one with no writer — is rejected
232	    here, before any byte is read and without ever waiting on it.  On
233	    success the descriptor's temporary non-blocking mode is cleared, so
234	    callers stream an ordinary blocking file.  On any rejection the
235	    descriptor is closed here, so no opened file is leaked by a failed
236	    confirmation.
237	    """
238	    try:
239	        opened = os.fstat(descriptor)
240	    except OSError as error:
241	        _close_quietly(descriptor)
242	        raise ConfirmationError(
243	            ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR, ConfirmStage.PROVE, error=error
244	        ) from error
245	    if not stat.S_ISREG(opened.st_mode) or (
246	        opened.st_dev,
247	        opened.st_ino,
248	    ) != (confirmed.st_dev, confirmed.st_ino):
249	        _close_quietly(descriptor)
250	        raise ConfirmationError(
251	            ConfirmReason.WRONG_IDENTITY, ConfirmStage.PROVE, status=opened
252	        )
253	    _clear_nonblocking(descriptor)
254	    return opened
255	
256	
257	class ConfirmedOpen(NamedTuple):
258	    """A successfully confirmed open.
259	
260	    ``descriptor`` is the open read-only descriptor (owned by the
261	    caller), ``confirmed`` is the pre-open no-follow inspection the
262	    descriptor was proved against, and ``opened`` is the descriptor's
263	    own ``fstat()`` result — same object identity, but carrying the
264	    size used while streaming.
265	    """
266	
267	    descriptor: int
268	    confirmed: os.stat_result
269	    opened: os.stat_result
270	
271	
272	def confirm_and_open_regular(
273	    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
274	    *,
275	    dir_fd: int | None = None,
276	    expected: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
277	) -> ConfirmedOpen:
278	    """Inspect, open without following links, and prove the descriptor.
279	
280	    Returns the open descriptor together with the pre-open inspection
281	    and the descriptor's own status.  The descriptor is owned by the
282	    caller; every failure path closes it.
283	    """
284	    confirmed_status = inspect_regular(path, dir_fd=dir_fd, expected=expected)
285	    descriptor = open_without_follow(path, dir_fd=dir_fd)
286	    opened = prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status)
287	    return ConfirmedOpen(descriptor, confirmed_status, opened)
288	
289	
290	def hash_descriptor(descriptor: int) -> str:
291	    """Stream ``descriptor`` in chunks and return its full SHA-256 digest.
292	
293	    The descriptor is wrapped with ``fdopen`` and released by the
294	    wrapper whether the read succeeds or raises (and closed if the
295	    wrapping itself fails), so a caller never has to reclaim it.
296	    """
297	    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
298	    try:
299	        stream = os.fdopen(descriptor, "rb")
300	    except BaseException:
301	        _close_quietly(descriptor)
302	        raise
303	    with stream:
304	        while True:
305	            chunk = stream.read(READ_CHUNK_SIZE)
306	            if not chunk:
307	                break
308	            hasher.update(chunk)
309	    return hasher.hexdigest()
310	
311	
312	def same_identity(left: os.stat_result, right: os.stat_result) -> bool:
313	    """Whether two stat results name the same object (device and inode)."""
314	    return (left.st_dev, left.st_ino) == (right.st_dev, right.st_ino)
315	
316	
317	def same_identity_size_mtime(
318	    left: os.stat_result, right: os.stat_result
319	) -> bool:
320	    """Whether both results describe the same unchanged file.
321	
322	    Beyond the object identity this compares the byte size and
323	    modification time (nanosecond precision), which import requires
324	    before and after a read so in-place rewrites, appends and truncation
325	    are rejected as well as replacements.
326	    """
327	    return (
328	        left.st_dev,
329	        left.st_ino,
330	        left.st_size,
331	        left.st_mtime_ns,
332	    ) == (
333	        right.st_dev,
334	        right.st_ino,
335	        right.st_size,
336	        right.st_mtime_ns,
337	    )
338	
339	
340	def _close_quietly(descriptor: int) -> None:
341	    try:
342	        os.close(descriptor)
343	    except OSError:
344	        pass
345

that turns a path into sample bytes:

* single-file import (``DatasetStore.add``),

   (or refused) immediately instead of making the caller wait for data,

3. The opened descriptor is ``fstat()``ed and proved to be a regular
   file carrying the exact ``(device, inode)`` identity that was
   confirmed (or, for the export copy, the identity recorded during the
   lookup): a different regular file renamed onto the path — even one
   with identical content, size and modification time — is rejected
   just like a symlink, even one pointing at the original file, and a
   named pipe or other non-regular object caught by the non-blocking
   open is rejected the same way.  Only then is the descriptor's
   blocking mode restored, so the files callers actually stream behave
   exactly like an ordinary blocking open.

What differs between entry points deliberately stays outside this
module:

* whether a path occupied by something else *after* a successful open
  still matters — import re-inspects the path once the read is done and
  requires the same file with the same size and mtime, while export
  keeps reading the already pinned descriptor (the path may be
  reoccupied without spoiling the confirmed bytes);
* the public exception type, wording and identifying information.

Failures are therefore reported as structured :class:`ConfirmationError`
reasons; each entry point translates them into its existing public
errors, preserving the path, digest and reason information callers rely
on.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import errno
import fcntl
import hashlib
import os
import stat
from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import Enum
from typing import NamedTuple

# Samples are streamed in fixed chunks, so large files never need memory
# for their whole content; every reader below uses the same chunk size.
READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 1024 * 1024

# Open without following a final symlink; 0 on platforms lacking the flag.
_O_NOFOLLOW = getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
# Open without waiting for a writer/reader or carrier: the descriptor is
# proved to be a regular file before any read, so an object swapped onto
# the path after the inspection — a named pipe with no writer in
# particular — is opened (and then rejected) immediately instead of
# making the confirmation wait for data.  Cleared again once the open is
# proved regular, so streaming sees an ordinary blocking descriptor.
_O_NONBLOCK = getattr(os, "O_NONBLOCK", 0)


class ConfirmStage(str, Enum):
    """Where in the confirm-then-open sequence a failure was detected."""

    INSPECT = "inspect"  # the no-follow lstat()/fstatat() before opening
    OPEN = "open"  # the O_NOFOLLOW open()
    PROVE = "prove"  # the fstat() of the freshly opened descriptor


class ConfirmReason(str, Enum):
    """What went wrong, independent of the caller's public wording."""

    ACCESS_ERROR = "access error"  # an underlying syscall failed; .error set
    NOT_REGULAR = "not a regular file"  # a non-symlink, non-regular object
    NOW_SYMLINK = "is now a symlink"  # the path became a final symlink
    WRONG_IDENTITY = "wrong identity"  # another object occupies the path


@dataclass
class ConfirmationError(Exception):
    """A path could not be confirmed as, or opened as, one stable file.

    ``status`` carries the inspection result when one was obtained, so a
    caller can tell symlinks from other non-regular objects; ``error``
    carries the underlying :class:`OSError` for access failures.
    """

    reason: ConfirmReason
    stage: ConfirmStage
    status: os.stat_result | None = None
    error: OSError | None = None

    def __str__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging only
        return f"{self.reason.value} at {self.stage.value}"


def inspect_regular(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    dir_fd: int | None = None,
    expected: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
) -> os.stat_result:
    """Inspect ``path`` without following a final symlink and confirm it.

    Returns the status of the confirmed regular file.  When ``dir_fd``
    is given, ``path`` is interpreted relative to that descriptor
    (``fstatat``); otherwise it is ``lstat()``ed directly.

    ``expected`` optionally carries the ``(device, inode)`` the binding
    must still carry — the identity recorded during the source-dir
    lookup when the export copy re-confirms a selected path.  A path
    that is a symlink, is not a regular file, or no longer carries the
    expected identity raises :class:`ConfirmationError` before anything
    is opened.
    """
    try:
        if dir_fd is None:
            status = os.lstat(path)
        else:
            status = os.stat(path, dir_fd=dir_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
    except OSError as error:
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, error=error
        ) from error
    if stat.S_ISLNK(status.st_mode):
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
        )
    if not stat.S_ISREG(status.st_mode):
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.NOT_REGULAR, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
        )
    if expected is not None and (status.st_dev, status.st_ino) != expected:
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.WRONG_IDENTITY, ConfirmStage.INSPECT, status=status
        )
    return status


def open_without_follow(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    dir_fd: int | None = None,
    nonblocking: bool = True,
) -> int:
    """Open ``path`` read-only with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, never following a link.

    With ``nonblocking`` (the default) the open also carries
    ``O_NONBLOCK``: it never waits for another process, so a named pipe
    (or other carrier) swapped onto the path in the gap after the
    inspection is opened immediately even with no writer present,
    rather than blocking before the descriptor can be proved.  Callers
    that pair this open with :func:`prove_opened_regular` get an
    ordinary blocking descriptor back once the open is proved regular.
    A final symlink swapped in after the inspection makes the open fail
    with ``ELOOP``, which is reported as
    :class:`ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK` rather than a generic access
    error; every other open failure carries the original
    :class:`OSError`.  The descriptor belongs to the caller on success.

    ``nonblocking=False`` restores the plain blocking
    ``O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW`` open for callers that deliberately keep the
    historical lookup-open semantics (the source-directory scan); such
    callers must not rely on the descriptor being proved here.
    """
    flags = os.O_RDONLY | _O_NOFOLLOW
    if nonblocking:
        flags |= _O_NONBLOCK
    try:
        return os.open(path, flags, dir_fd=dir_fd)
    except OSError as error:
        reason = (
            ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK
            if error.errno == errno.ELOOP
            else ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR
        )
        raise ConfirmationError(
            reason, ConfirmStage.OPEN, error=error
        ) from error


def _clear_nonblocking(descriptor: int) -> None:
    """Restore ordinary blocking semantics on a proved descriptor.

    The non-blocking flag only existed to keep the open itself from
    waiting on a swapped non-regular carrier; streaming the now-proved
    regular file must behave like an ordinary blocking open.  Clearing
    access flags on a regular file never blocks.
    """
    try:
        flags = fcntl.fcntl(descriptor, fcntl.F_GETFL)
        fcntl.fcntl(descriptor, fcntl.F_SETFL, flags & ~os.O_NONBLOCK)
    except OSError as error:
        _close_quietly(descriptor)
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR, ConfirmStage.PROVE, error=error
        ) from error


def prove_opened_regular(
    descriptor: int, confirmed: os.stat_result
) -> os.stat_result:
    """Prove ``descriptor`` is the confirmed regular file itself.

    The descriptor is ``fstat()``ed and must be a regular file carrying
    ``confirmed``'s ``(device, inode)``; this covers the object that is
    actually read, not just one look at the path before it was opened.
    A named pipe or other non-regular object that the non-blocking open
    let through after a swap — even one with no writer — is rejected
    here, before any byte is read and without ever waiting on it.  On
    success the descriptor's temporary non-blocking mode is cleared, so
    callers stream an ordinary blocking file.  On any rejection the
    descriptor is closed here, so no opened file is leaked by a failed
    confirmation.
    """
    try:
        opened = os.fstat(descriptor)
    except OSError as error:
        _close_quietly(descriptor)
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR, ConfirmStage.PROVE, error=error
        ) from error
    if not stat.S_ISREG(opened.st_mode) or (
        opened.st_dev,
        opened.st_ino,
    ) != (confirmed.st_dev, confirmed.st_ino):
        _close_quietly(descriptor)
        raise ConfirmationError(
            ConfirmReason.WRONG_IDENTITY, ConfirmStage.PROVE, status=opened
        )
    _clear_nonblocking(descriptor)
    return opened


class ConfirmedOpen(NamedTuple):
    """A successfully confirmed open.

    ``descriptor`` is the open read-only descriptor (owned by the
    caller), ``confirmed`` is the pre-open no-follow inspection the
    descriptor was proved against, and ``opened`` is the descriptor's
    own ``fstat()`` result — same object identity, but carrying the
    size used while streaming.
    """

    descriptor: int
    confirmed: os.stat_result
    opened: os.stat_result


def confirm_and_open_regular(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    dir_fd: int | None = None,
    expected: tuple[int, int] | None = None,
) -> ConfirmedOpen:
    """Inspect, open without following links, and prove the descriptor.

    Returns the open descriptor together with the pre-open inspection
    and the descriptor's own status.  The descriptor is owned by the
    caller; every failure path closes it.
    """
    confirmed_status = inspect_regular(path, dir_fd=dir_fd, expected=expected)
    descriptor = open_without_follow(path, dir_fd=dir_fd)
    opened = prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status)
    return ConfirmedOpen(descriptor, confirmed_status, opened)


def hash_descriptor(descriptor: int) -> str:
    """Stream ``descriptor`` in chunks and return its full SHA-256 digest.

    The descriptor is wrapped with ``fdopen`` and released by the
    wrapper whether the read succeeds or raises (and closed if the
    wrapping itself fails), so a caller never has to reclaim it.
    """
    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
    try:
        stream = os.fdopen(descriptor, "rb")
    except BaseException:
        _close_quietly(descriptor)
        raise
    with stream:
        while True:
            chunk = stream.read(READ_CHUNK_SIZE)
            if not chunk:
                break
            hasher.update(chunk)
    return hasher.hexdigest()


def same_identity(left: os.stat_result, right: os.stat_result) -> bool:
    """Whether two stat results name the same object (device and inode)."""
    return (left.st_dev, left.st_ino) == (right.st_dev, right.st_ino)


def same_identity_size_mtime(
    left: os.stat_result, right: os.stat_result
) -> bool:
    """Whether both results describe the same unchanged file.

    Beyond the object identity this compares the byte size and
    modification time (nanosecond precision), which import requires
    before and after a read so in-place rewrites, appends and truncation
    are rejected as well as replacements.
    """
    return (
        left.st_dev,
        left.st_ino,
        left.st_size,
        left.st_mtime_ns,
    ) == (
        right.st_dev,
        right.st_ino,
        right.st_size,
        right.st_mtime_ns,
    )


def _close_quietly(descriptor: int) -> None:
    try:
        os.close(descriptor)
    except OSError:
        pass

338	            for entry in entries:
339	                try:
340	                    is_file = entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False)
341	                    is_dir = (
342	                        not is_file
343	                        and recursive
344	                        and entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
345	                    )
346	                except OSError as error:
347	                    raise ValueError(
348	                        f"cannot inspect entry {directory / entry.name}: {error}"
349	                    ) from error
350	                found.append((entry.name, is_file, is_dir))
351	            return found

353	        def walk(
354	            directory: Path,
355	            rel_prefix: str,
356	            parent_fd: int,
357	            entries: list[tuple[str, bool, bool]],
358	        ) -> None:
359	            for name, is_file, is_dir in entries:
360	                if is_file:
361	                    if Path(name).suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS:
362	                        rel_paths.append(rel_prefix + name)
363	                elif is_dir:
364	                    subdirectory = directory / name
365	                    # Open the confirmed subdirectory through the pinned
366	                    # parent with O_NOFOLLOW and scan the descriptor
367	                    # itself: a symlink swapped onto the path by now fails
368	                    # the whole import here, and the link target is never
369	                    # scanned.
370	                    try:
371	                        child_fd = self._open_real_directory(
372	                            name, parent_fd, subdirectory
373	                        )
374	                    except OSError as error:
375	                        raise ValueError(
376	                            f"cannot scan directory {subdirectory}: {error}"
377	                        ) from error
378	                    try:
379	                        child_entries = classify(subdirectory, child_fd)
380	                        confirmed_dirs.append(subdirectory)
381	                        walk(
382	                            subdirectory,
383	                            rel_prefix + name + "/",
384	                            child_fd,
385	                            child_entries,
386	                        )
387	                    finally:
388	                        os.close(child_fd)
389	
390	        try:
391	            root_fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
392	        except OSError as error:
393	            raise ValueError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
394	        try:
395	            walk(root, "", root_fd, classify(root, root))
396	        finally:
397	            os.close(root_fd)
398	        # Unicode code point order on the slash-separated relative path.
399	        rel_paths.sort()
400	        return rel_paths, confirmed_dirs

402	    @staticmethod
403	    def _open_real_directory(name: str, dir_fd: int | None, path: Path) -> int:
404	        """Open a confirmed directory, refusing a symlink swapped onto it.
405	
406	        The open uses ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW`` — relative to the
407	        pinned parent descriptor when ``dir_fd`` is given — so a symbolic
408	        link (or any non-directory) that replaced the confirmed directory
409	        is never descended through.  A symlink swap raises the import's
410	        "directory changed" error naming the replaced path; any other
411	        open failure propagates as the underlying :class:`OSError`.
412	        """
413	        try:
414	            return os.open(name, _DIRECTORY_OPEN_FLAGS, dir_fd=dir_fd)
415	        except OSError as error:
416	            # Linux reports a symlink opened with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY
417	            # as ENOTDIR rather than ELOOP, so confirm via lstat() either
418	            # way.
419	            if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
420	                try:
421	                    current = os.lstat(path)
422	                except OSError:
423	                    current = None
424	                if current is not None and stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
425	                    raise ValueError(
426	                        f"directory changed during import: {path} "
427	                        "is now a symbolic link"
428	                    ) from error
429	            raise

431	    @staticmethod
432	    def _raise_if_now_symlink(directory: Path) -> None:
433	        """Fail if a previously confirmed real directory is now a symlink.
434	
435	        A path that vanished is left to the candidate reads (or ignored
436	        when the directory held no candidates); only the symlink swap is
437	        rejected here, because following the link would import the target's
438	        images against the no-symlinked-directories rule.
439	        """
440	        try:
441	            current = os.lstat(directory)
442	        except OSError:
443	            return
444	        if stat.S_ISLNK(current.st_mode):
445	            raise ValueError(
446	                f"directory changed during import: {directory} "
447	                "is now a symbolic link"
448	            )

450	    def _read_candidate(
451	        self, path: Path, rel_path: str
452	    ) -> tuple[str, Path, str, int]:
453	        """Read one candidate in full, verifying identity/size/mtime around it.
454	
455	        Returns ``(rel_path, absolute_path, digest, size)``.  A mismatch or
456	        read failure raises before the batch is committed.
457	
458	        Every ancestor directory of the candidate is re-opened from the
459	        source root with ``O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW``, each relative to its
460	        pinned parent, and the candidate itself is opened relative to its
461	        pinned parent directory: a subdirectory replaced by a symbolic
462	        link since the scan fails the whole import here, and the link
463	        target's images are never opened — no matter when the swap lands.
464	        """
465	        parts = Path(rel_path).parts
466	        root = path
467	        for _ in parts:
468	            root = root.parent
469	        try:
470	            fd = self._open_real_directory(str(root), None, root)
471	        except OSError as error:
472	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}") from error
473	        try:
474	            ancestor = root
475	            for part in parts[:-1]:
476	                ancestor = ancestor / part
477	                try:
478	                    next_fd = self._open_real_directory(part, fd, ancestor)
479	                except OSError as error:
480	                    raise ValueError(
481	                        f"cannot read {rel_path}: {error}"
482	                    ) from error
483	                os.close(fd)
484	                fd = next_fd
485	            digest, size = self._read_stable(
486	                path, rel_path, dir_fd=fd, name=parts[-1]
487	            )
488	        finally:
489	            os.close(fd)
490	        return rel_path, path, digest, size
491	
492	    @staticmethod
493	    def _read_stable(
494	        path: Path,
495	        display: str,
496	        *,
497	        dir_fd: int | None = None,
498	        name: str | None = None,
499	    ) -> tuple[str, int]:
500	        """Read one file in full and return ``(digest, size)`` for it.
501	
502	        The digest and size are guaranteed to describe the same stable
503	        regular file: the path is lstat()ed without following symlinks
504	        and opened with ``O_NOFOLLOW``, the opened descriptor is
505	        fstat()ed to prove it is the inode that was confirmed, and the
506	        path is lstat()ed again after the read, requiring the same
507	        object with the same size and modification time.  Any identity,
508	        size or modification-time change — in-place rewrites, appends,
509	        truncation, delete-and-recreate, or replacing the path with
510	        another file, even one with identical content, size and mtime —
511	        fails with the path and reason, as do a vanishing path, a
512	        non-regular file and any open or read error.
513	
514	        The confirm/open/prove rule itself lives in :mod:`confirmed`
515	        and is shared with the source-directory export; only the
516	        post-read stability requirement and the import wording are
517	        specific to this entry point.
518	
519	        When ``dir_fd`` and ``name`` are given (whole-directory import),
520	        the pre-open inspection and the post-read re-inspection stay on
521	        the path, but the open itself is ``name`` relative to the pinned
522	        parent directory descriptor: an ancestor directory replaced by a
523	        symbolic link can never redirect the open into the link target.
524	        """
525	        try:
526	            if dir_fd is None:
527	                opened_file = confirmed.confirm_and_open_regular(path)
528	            else:
529	                confirmed_status = confirmed.inspect_regular(path)
530	                descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=dir_fd)
531	                opened_file = confirmed.ConfirmedOpen(
532	                    descriptor,
533	                    confirmed_status,
534	                    confirmed.prove_opened_regular(descriptor, confirmed_status),
535	                )
536	        except confirmed.ConfirmationError as failure:
537	            raise _import_confirmation_error(failure, display) from failure
538	        try:
539	            digest = confirmed.hash_descriptor(opened_file.descriptor)
540	        except OSError as error:
541	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
542	        # Import, unlike export, also requires the path itself to still
543	        # name the same unchanged file after the read: an in-place
544	        # rewrite, append, truncation or replacement that landed while
545	        # the bytes were streamed must not register a digest/size pair
546	        # that never coexisted.
547	        try:
548	            after = os.lstat(path)
549	        except OSError as error:
550	            raise ValueError(f"cannot read {display}: {error}") from error
551	        if not confirmed.same_identity_size_mtime(opened_file.confirmed, after):
552	            raise ValueError(
553	                f"file changed during import: {display} "
554	                "(identity, size or modification time changed)"
555	            )
556	        return digest, opened_file.confirmed.st_size

562	        labels = Counter(item["label"] or "unlabeled" for item in items)

565	            "bytes": sum(item["size"] for item in items),
566	            "labels": dict(sorted(labels.items())),

569	    def find_by_label(self, label: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
570	        """List samples currently registered under one exact category label.
571	
572	        Matching is exact on the current manifest label: case, surrounding
573	        whitespace and path separators are all kept literally, so ``"cat"``
574	        never matches ``"Cat"`` or ``"cat "``.  The empty string queries
575	        unlabeled samples — records whose stored label is ``None`` or ``""``
576	        — and every matching record's label is reported uniformly as
577	        ``None``.  A genuine class literally named ``"unlabeled"`` is
578	        queried with that text and never mixed with unlabeled samples,
579	        unlike :meth:`summary` which merges them under one display key.
580	
581	        Each record provides the full SHA-256 digest, the source path saved
582	        at first registration, the byte size and the current label;
583	        records are sorted ascending by full digest and ``count`` always
584	        equals the list length.  The query reads the registered records
585	        only — it never opens a source file, and saved split plans' old
586	        labels are neither matched nor rewritten — so a moved, deleted or
587	        unreadable source is still found, and a batch update or undo
588	        committed before the call is immediately reflected.
589	        """
590	        if not isinstance(label, str):
591	            raise BatchError("query label must be a string")
592	        want_unlabeled = label == ""
593	        samples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
594	        self.initialize()
595	        with self._locked():
596	            items = self._read()["items"]
597	        for item in items:
598	            stored = item.get("label")
599	            if want_unlabeled:
600	                if not (stored is None or stored == ""):
601	                    continue
602	                current = None
603	            else:
604	                if stored != label:
605	                    continue
606	                current = stored
607	            samples.append(
608	                {
609	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
610	                    "source": item["source"],
611	                    "size": item["size"],
612	                    "label": current,
613	                }
614	            )
615	        samples.sort(key=lambda sample: sample["sha256"])
616	        return {"label": label, "count": len(samples), "samples": samples}

634	    def submit_batch_file(self, path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:

636	        try:
637	            data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

642	    def submit_batch(self, data: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
643	        """Validate and apply a batch label update.
644	
645	        Parsing happens before the lock; inside the lock the submission
646	        runs through clearly separated stages, each with one job:
647	
648	        1. **Unknown samples** — every named digest must be registered; the
649	           first unknown one rejects the batch with nothing written.
650	        2. **Number identity** — a batch number already in history either
651	           replays the first submission's result (same content) or is a
652	           conflict (different content); neither touches the manifest.
653	        3. **Verification/classification** — each current label is read
654	           once: an expected-old mismatch rejects the batch, and the same
655	           reading decides whether that record actually changes.
656	        4. **Application** — only records classified as changed are
657	           mutated; if none are, the batch occupies no number and writes
658	           no history.
659	        5. **History and save** — the entry and result are assembled from
660	           the applied records, and manifest plus history commit together
661	           through the journal.
662	
663	        No stage mutates anything before every earlier stage has passed, so
664	        a rejection can neither leave partially updated samples nor a
665	        partial history entry.
666	        """
667	        number, records = parse_batch_file(data)
668	        with self._locked(create=True):
669	            manifest = self._read()
670	            history = self._read_history()
671	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
672	
673	            # Stage 1: every record must name a registered sample.
674	            reject_unknown_samples(records, items.__contains__)
675	
676	            # Stage 2: a known number is replayed or conflicts; a fresh
677	            # number proceeds without examining the current labels.
678	            existing = next(
679	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),
680	                None,
681	            )
682	            replay = resolve_re_submission(number, records, existing)
683	            if replay is not None:
684	                return replay
685	
686	            # Stage 3: verify expected old labels and classify changed vs
687	            # unchanged in a single current-label pass.
688	            resolutions = verify_records(
689	                records,
690	                lambda digest: normalize_label(items[digest].get("label")),
691	            )
692	
693	            # Stage 4: apply is the only mutation.  No changes at all
694	            # occupies no batch number and writes no history.
695	            if not any(resolution.changed for resolution in resolutions):
696	                return no_changes_result(number, len(records))
697	            applied_records = apply_resolutions(resolutions, items)
698	
699	            # Stage 5: assemble history, then save manifest and history
700	            # together through the journal.
701	            entry = build_history_entry(number, applied_records)
702	            history["batches"].append(entry)
703	            self._commit(manifest, history)
704	            return result_payload(number, "applied", applied_records)
705	
706	    def undo_batch(self, number: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
707	        """Undo a successful batch by number.
708	
709	        Only samples the batch actually changed are checked: each must have
710	        the same label revision it had right after the batch (no later
711	        modification, even one that restored the same label).  Repeated
712	        undos are idempotent and do not add history.
713	
714	        Integrity comes before either verdict: the target batch must list
715	        every sample exactly once and carry a sound pinned revision on each
716	        record.  A duplicated digest or a bad row rejects the undo even when
717	        the batch is already marked undone, so corruption is never hidden
718	        behind an ``already-undone`` success or confused with a sample
719	        modified after the batch.
720	        """
721	        with self._locked(create=True):
722	            manifest = self._read()
723	            history = self._read_history()
724	            entry = next(
725	                (entry for entry in history["batches"] if entry["batch"] == number),
726	                None,
727	            )
728	            if entry is None:
729	                raise BatchError(f"unknown batch number: {number!r}")
730	
731	            # Validate the target batch's integrity — one row per sample and
732	            # sound pinned revisions — before the already-undone
733	            # short-circuit and the later-modification checks: a duplicated
734	            # or corrupt history record is refusal, not an undo, a no-op or
735	            # an unknown batch, and nothing is rewritten.
736	            require_intact_history_records(entry)
737	            require_intact_history_revisions(entry)
738	
739	            if entry["undone"]:
740	                return {"batch": number, "status": "already-undone", "restored": 0}
741	
742	            items = {item["sha256"]: item for item in manifest["items"]}
743	            for record in entry["records"]:
744	                if not record["changed"]:
745	                    continue
746	                item = items.get(record["sha256"])
747	                if item is None:
748	                    raise BatchError(
749	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
750	                        "is no longer in the manifest"
751	                    )
752	                current = normalize_label(item.get("label"))
753	                # record["rev"] is now known to be a genuine non-negative
754	                # integer, so a boolean/decimal/string can never compare
755	                # equal to the sample's current revision.
756	                if item_revision(item) != record["rev"] or current != record["new"]:
757	                    raise BatchError(
758	                        f"cannot undo batch {number!r}: sample {record['sha256']} "
759	                        "was modified after the batch"
760	                    )
761	
762	            restored = 0
763	            for record in entry["records"]:
764	                if not record["changed"]:
765	                    continue
766	                item = items[record["sha256"]]
767	                item["label"] = record["old"]
768	                item["rev"] = item_revision(item) + 1
769	                restored += 1
770	
771	            entry["undone"] = True
772	            entry["undone_at"] = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
773	            self._commit(manifest, history)
774	            return {"batch": number, "status": "undone", "restored": restored}
775	
776	    def history(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
777	        """Return successful batch entries in submission order."""
778	        with self._locked():
779	            return self._read_history()["batches"]

785	    @contextmanager
786	    def _workspace_lock(self):
787	        """Exclusive workspace lock for check-and-write transactions.
788	
789	        ``flock`` is advisory but sufficient for local processes: holders
790	        serialize, so every read-modify-write observes the state left by the
791	        previous completed operation.
792	        """
793	        self.state_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
794	        descriptor = os.open(self.lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
795	        try:
796	            fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
797	            yield
798	        finally:
799	            try:
800	                fcntl.flock(descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
801	            finally:
802	                os.close(descriptor)
803	
804	    @contextmanager
805	    def _locked(self, *, create: bool = False):
806	        """Hold the workspace lock and finish any leftover prepared journal.
807	
808	        Recovery runs once the lock is held, so a long-lived process that
809	        only imports, queries or creates plans still installs the prepared
810	        transaction of a process that crashed on this machine, without
811	        needing to reopen the workspace.
812	
813	        Read callers leave ``create`` false: on a workspace whose state
814	        directory does not yet exist there is no journal to finish and
815	        nothing for a writer to hold, so the query proceeds (and fails or
816	        reports empty exactly as before) without materializing one.
817	        """
818	        if not create and not self.state_directory.exists():
819	            yield
820	            return
821	        with self._workspace_lock():
822	            self._recover_transaction_locked()
823	            yield
824	
825	    def _recover_if_needed(self) -> None:
826	        """Finish a prepared transaction left by a crashed process."""
827	        if not self.transaction_path.exists():
828	            return
829	        with self._locked():
830	            pass
831	
832	    def _recover_transaction_locked(self) -> None:
833	        if not self.transaction_path.exists():
834	            return
835	        try:
836	            journal = json.loads(self.transaction_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
837	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
838	            raise BatchError(f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}") from error
839	        manifest = journal.get("manifest")
840	        history = journal.get("batches")
841	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
842	            raise BatchError("cannot recover interrupted transaction: journal is malformed")
843	        # Only install a coherent, fully valid pair, so recovery can never
844	        # replace the committed manifest with a structurally broken sample
845	        # list (a missing field, a bad field type or a duplicated digest):
846	        # the check runs before either file is rewritten, leaving both the
847	        # last committed registration and its history untouched.
848	        try:
849	            validate_manifest(manifest)
850	        except ManifestError as error:
851	            raise BatchError(
852	                f"cannot recover interrupted transaction: {error}"
853	            ) from error
854	        validate_history(history)
855	        # Idempotent installs: both files end up at the journal's version.
856	        self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
857	        self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)
858	        try:
859	            self.transaction_path.unlink()
860	        except OSError:
861	            pass
862	
863	    def _commit(self, manifest: dict[str, Any], history: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
864	        """Atomically install the new manifest and history together.
865	
866	        A write-ahead journal holding both full payloads is written and
867	        fsynced first; a crash at any point leaves enough to redo the
868	        missing install on the next open, so the two files never disagree.
869	        """
870	        journal = {"manifest": manifest, "batches": history}
871	        self._write_json_atomic(self.transaction_path, journal)
872	        self._write_json_atomic(self.manifest_path, manifest)
873	        self._write_json_atomic(self.batches_path, history)
874	        try:
875	            self.transaction_path.unlink()
876	        except OSError:
877	            pass
878	
879	    def _read_history(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
880	        if not self.batches_path.exists():
881	            return empty_history()
882	        try:
883	            data = json.loads(self.batches_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
884	        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
885	            raise BatchError(f"cannot read batch history: {error}") from error
886	        return validate_history(data)

892	    def create_split(
893	        self, name: str, seed: int, ratios: list[float | int | str | Fraction]
894	    ) -> SplitPlanResult:
895	        """Create (or reuse) a named train/validation/test plan.
896	
897	        The plan snapshots every sample currently in the manifest.  A
898	        second call with the same name returns the stored plan unchanged
899	        when the inputs match; otherwise it reports a name conflict.
900	        """
901	        validate_name(name)
902	        if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
903	            raise SplitError(f"Seed must be an integer, got {seed!r}")
904	        fraction_ratios = validate_ratios(ratios)
905	
906	        self.initialize()
907	        plan_path = self._split_path(name)
908	
909	        with self._locked(create=True):
910	            # Sample identities and labels are read from one complete
911	            # manifest state, so a batch committing concurrently is observed
912	            # either entirely (all its label changes) or not at all.
913	            items = self._read()["items"]
914	            # assign() validates identities and performs the stratification.
915	            assignment = assign(items, fraction_ratios, seed)
916	
917	            snapshot = [
918	                {
919	                    "sha256": item["sha256"],
920	                    "label": item.get("label"),
921	                    "source": item.get("source"),
922	                }
923	                for item in sorted(items, key=lambda item: item["sha256"])
924	            ]
925	            plan_payload = self._build_plan(
926	                name, seed, fraction_ratios, snapshot, assignment
927	            )
928	
929	            # The check-and-create is atomic under the same lock, so among
930	            # concurrent creations of one name exactly one reports success;

from __future__ import annotations

import errno

from . import confirmed
from .manifest import ManifestError, validate_manifest
from .batches import (
    BatchError,
    apply_resolutions,
    build_history_entry,

    item_revision,
